top_choice_rationale: P001 (B048, Melitz and Helpman) is the only prize proposal on the slate, and it is also my own round-2 preferred configuration. Melitz (2003) is an identifiable originating model. It moved trade theory from the representative firm to selection into exporting and reallocation across firms, which is a distinct channel for the gains from trade. Helpman's exporting-versus-FDI work with Melitz and Yeaple makes him the natural second name. The qualitative predictions (exporter premia, selection, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm-level data for over twenty years. Credit divides cleanly between two names. The main weaknesses are the priority question around Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum and the dependence of welfare magnitudes on functional form. I judge that a citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism and the gains-from-trade framework handles both adequately. These weaknesses do not outweigh the merit of the discovery, so I rank an award above no award. I do not treat the unanimous support for P001 as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile regarding Melitz or Helpman. I disclose, without adjudicating, co-authorship and institutional ties with committee colleagues Krusell, Boppart and Friberg, and my role as chair. I also note that my round-1 preference for B001 has since moved to B048.
